content.summary: Bounded execution contract for assessing security posture against selected security blocks and threat models.
acceptanceCriteria: Every selected security-domain block is assessed.
Every finding references a specific block, acceptance criterion, or constraint.
No fabricated vulnerabilities — all findings traceable to block evidence or constraint violations.
Threat surface summary derived from block failureModes, not generic lists.
Output severity levels match block gapSignal severity definitions.
invariants: All findings must always trace back to specific block evidence or constraint violations.
Output severity levels must always match the defined gap signal severity definitions.
mustNot: Do not fabricate vulnerabilities not supported by codebase evidence.
Do not produce generic findings not grounded in specific blocks.
failureModes: Fabricating vulnerabilities not supported by codebase evidence — false positive threats.
Missing critical attack surfaces covered by selected security blocks — false negative assessment.
Reporting only obvious issues while missing subtle constraint violations.
Producing generic OWASP list instead of project-specific findings grounded in blocks.

content.summary: Bounded execution contract for scoring a generated artifact against rubric criteria and identifying sections that need repair.
acceptanceCriteria: Overall score is computed from weighted criteria.
Failed checks identify specific artifact sections for repair.
Score is reproducible — same artifact and same rubric produce the same score.
invariants: Every artifact must always be evaluated against its corresponding rubric.
The evaluation process must never produce inconsistent scores for the same artifact and rubric.
failureModes: Subjective check evaluation — human-judgment checks scored inconsistently across runs.
Missing rubric for artifact type — evaluation skipped entirely.
Rubric criteria too broad to produce actionable repair targets.
Evaluation score does not correlate with actual artifact usefulness.

content.summary: Server-managed session model for B2B SaaS with secure cookie storage, refresh token rotation, and tenant-scoped session lifecycle.
invariants: Sessions are always tenant-scoped. A session for workspace A cannot access workspace B.
Refresh token reuse invalidates the entire session family.
Revoked sessions return 401 on the next request, with zero delay.
Session creation requires verified identity (email verification or OAuth callback).
procedures: Create session on successful login. Store session ID, user ID, workspace ID, created_at, expires_at, refresh_token_hash.
On each request, validate session cookie, check expiry, verify workspace scope.
On refresh, rotate the refresh token. Invalidate the old token. Extend session expiry.
On logout, delete the session record. Clear the cookie. Log the event.
On password change, revoke all active sessions for the user.
failureModes: Session fixation. Mitigate by regenerating session ID after login.
Refresh token theft. Mitigate by rotating on every use and invalidating reuse.
Cross-tenant session leakage. Mitigate by binding every session to a workspace ID.
Session storage failure. Mitigate by failing closed — deny access if session cannot be verified.
